messages:
jess-support: Customer ac-9876 reported a burst of 429s during a 3-minute backfill at ~13:02 UTC. They say requests started succeeding, then all turned 429 with headers showing zero burst credits. Can we triage and share short-term mitigations?

ingest-bot: Alert: route=/v1/generate spike detected +115% over baseline, 429 rate increased. Incident id: alert-7852.

customer-ops: We saw ~2.1k requests in ~180s from their backfill job, ~10 concurrent streams. They sent sample response headers (sanitized) below.

jess-support: Sample customer response headers: `HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests` `x-redwood-burst-credits: 0` `x-redwood-burst-last-refill: 1680000000` `x-rate-limit-limit: 100` `x-rate-limit-remaining: 0` `x-request-id: rq_1234abcd`

sam-eng: Thanks. Two quick asks: 1) do we have the customer's request pattern (concurrency + token distribution)? 2) can you share a short repro (curl loop) so I can run it against staging with their account? Also, check whether they were using retries without jitter which can amplify drain.

jess-support: Concurrency ~10, avg tokens per request small (~30 tokens). They were sending 10 parallel worker processes from a k8s job with no jitter. Repro script below (sanitized):

```
for i in {1..1000}; do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwoodai.com/v1/generate \n    -H "Authorization: Bearer xxxxxx" \n    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n    -d '{"model":"rwd-sm-1","input":"short prompt"}' &
done
wait
```

tanvi-sre: This pattern will consume the short-term cushion quickly because many parallel short requests have poor amortized prefix reuse. Short-term mitigations:
- Reduce parallel workers to 2-3 for the backfill.
- Add exponential backoff with full jitter on 429s (example below).
- We can temporarily increase their cushion (route-level additional credits) for 1 hour while they rework backfill.

sam-eng: Example retry strategy (python/pseudocode):

```
import random, time
for attempt in range(6):
  r = requests.post(url, headers=hdr, json=payload)
  if r.status_code != 429:
    break
  sleep = (0.1 * (2 ** attempt)) + random.random() * 0.1
  time.sleep(sleep)
```

sam-eng: For reproducible testing, run a controlled 10-thread loop with a 50ms jitter between requests; that usually exposes whether smoothing/fractional refill helps.

jess-support: How do we flip smoothing/fractional refill for the customer? They asked for a config/API way they can control.

tanvi-sre: We can enable account smoothing on the backend or via Console: Customer > Usage > Burst settings. Internal admin API (for ops) example: `POST /admin/v1/accounts/ac-9876/burst_config` with body `{"smoothing": true, "window_seconds": 60, "fractional_refill": true, "refill_rate": 0.25}`. Smoothing will spread credit consumption across the window and allow fractional/top-up behavior instead of discrete lumps.

tanvi-sre: Recommendation (short-term): enable smoothing + fractional_refill, set window_seconds=60 and refill_rate ~0.2-0.3 so their short bursts recover faster. Also set a temporary cushion: +2x credits for 1 hour.

support-bot: Action taken: temporary cushion applied to ac-9876 until 2026-03-20T14:10:00Z. Ticket #SUP-1129.

sam-eng: Long-term suggestions for customers with heavy backfills: prefer fewer concurrent streams, batch per-request tokens (combine small reqs if possible), or use a dedicated reserved capacity (Redwood Dedicated) for sustained high throughput jobs.

jess-support: I informed customer we're applying a temporary cushion and recommending the backoff + smoothing changes. They asked for repro steps to validate — I gave them the curl loop + the python retry snippet.

customer-ops: We'll follow up with the customer to confirm whether the temporary cushion stopped the 429s. Also scheduling a short tech call to review backfill strategy.

sam-eng: I'll run the repro in staging with their pattern and verify the smoothing flags behavior. If smoothing doesn't make a visible difference, we'll consider fractional refill tweaks and a small permanent cushion. Assigning follow-up to @tanvi-sre and @sam-eng.

jess-support: Closing notes: root cause is concurrent short-request backfill burning through the short-term credit reservoir. Mitigation path = temporary cushion + smoothing + client-side concurrency/backoff changes. Will update ticket SUP-1129 after testing. :white_check_mark:
